question: Does the strong reversal across Session A/B and execution order in frozen P1R reflect structured nuisance state large enough to make the A/B/C incremental estimand underidentified, or is the instability specifically associated with ANL64 plan/residual intervention?

audit_tests.T1_global_session_shift: For each arm/workload, compare Session B versus Session A medians. Test whether direction is shared across arms rather than specific to ANL64 arms.
audit_tests.T2_order_association: Within each workload, examine metric association with preregistered cell order across sessions and with global execution order across all 12 cells.
audit_tests.T3_within_cell_attempt_drift: Examine monotonic attempt-index trends within each cell to detect short-horizon execution-history/nonstationarity.
audit_tests.T4_arm_by_session_interaction: Compare session shifts for A, B and C. Determine whether B/C instability materially exceeds the canonical A shift.
audit_tests.T5_contrast_stability: Recompute B/A, C/B and C/A separately by session and quantify sign/materiality reversals.
audit_tests.T6_identifiability: Assess whether session/order variation is large relative to treatment contrasts and whether the existing counterbalance permits unique attribution.

CONFOUNDED_UNDERIDENTIFIED: A canonical control itself shows large session/order shifts in the same direction as B/C
session/order effect magnitude is comparable to or larger than one or more treatment contrasts
current design lacks independent telemetry or enough randomized blocks to identify the nuisance mechanism
ANL64_SPECIFIC_INSTABILITY: canonical A remains stable across sessions/order
large reversals are concentrated in B/C
B/C interaction exceeds global session/order shift
treatment-specific instability remains after conditioning on observed order/session factors
decision_rule.NO_DECISION: If evidence cannot support either pattern without importing unobserved assumptions.
